# Synthetic mapping-specification samples (fully fictional)

> **These fixtures are calibration examples, not the list of supported styles.**
> They exist to (1) regression-test what the import already reads and (2) show the kind of
> variety to expect. The import skill is generic: conventions (index base, array notation,
> null rule, date dialect, scope of conditions...) are discovered per document into a
> *profile* and asked about when the evidence is thin; no style is hard-coded. Real
> specifications will be more heterogeneous (prose-only Word, no JSON Schema, rules
> scattered across sheets...). Keep one fixture out of any tuning and use it only to
> evaluate generalisation; new styles are added as new fixtures, never by special-casing.

Five workbooks that reproduce the *layout, notation and register* of five recurring specification styles for JSON -> JSON transformations. Domains, fields, codes, people and values are invented. All files are in English.

| Folder | Style | Fictional flow | Rules | Deliberate features (see the `.truth.md` of each folder) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `wb1_reservation_task` | A | reservations -> housekeeping task event | 21 | two bands, `Y/N`, yellow rows, answered + unanswered review dialogue, vertical merges, 1-based segment rows `[1]/[2]`, `||` with unbalanced quotes, missing lookup table, non-existent source field, payload pasted one line per cell |
| `wb2_stock_ledger` | B | stock movements -> inventory ledger | 20 | legend + fills by transformation type, `Y/Yes/N/No`, **file name / Version sheet / "updated in version" disagree**, `Do Not Map` with rule present, `N` + "reject if null", samples contradicting rules, repeated separator in composite id |
| `wb3_enrolment_seat` | C | course enrolments -> timetable seats | 21 | one sheet per verb, `M/O/C` (C undefined), **struck-through rows (only workbook)**, `OR`/`AND` without precedence, mixed array notation, date dialects |
| `wb4_loan_notice` | D+I | library loans -> reminder notices | 25 | banded sections with conditions only in the title, em-dash for "no source", vertical merges, prose rules, missing lookup, blue example text, red unanswered question |
| `wb5_rental_billing` | K+L | equipment rentals -> billing request | 19 | numbered rows, packed-text parsing, `[2]` vs "index [3]", qualifier-filtered arrays, existence tests, repeated-separator id, JSON sample sheets |

Each folder contains:
- `<workbook>.xlsx` - the specification (real formatting, not described formatting);
- `<slug>.input.schema.json`, `<slug>.output.schema.json` - JSON Schema (draft 2020-12);
- `<slug>.truth.md` - unambiguous interpretation of every rule, implicit assumptions, deliberate ambiguities with their resolution;
- `<slug>.profile.json` - declared conventions (index base, array notation, mandatory vocabulary, date dialect, null rule, lookup tables);
- `tests/caseN.in.json` / `caseN.out.json` - three input/output pairs generated by a reference implementation of the truth file and validated against both schemas (each folder has a null-heavy case and an else-branch case).

## Anonymisation check (final scan)
Scanned: cell text of every sheet, sheet names, workbook metadata (author, last modified by, title, company, application properties), file names, schemas, truth files, profiles and test files (55 files).
- Terms checked: company, product and system names, message and interface names, people names, real-looking identifiers, real field/entity names, local paths and e-mail-like strings.
- Result of the final scan: **0 occurrences**.
- Metadata: author and last-modified-by are the neutral string `synthetic-generator`; no company, manager or template path is stored.

## Heterogeneous set (formats and styles beyond the first five)

Added to keep the reader honest: other media (Word, PDF, scan), no schema, rules in prose, rules in
requirement tables, rules in pseudo-code, several mappings per document, conventions declared up front. Same rules as above:
fully fictional, one `.truth.md` per folder, anonymised metadata.

| Folder | Medium / style | Fictional flow | Rules | Deliberate features |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `wb6_prose_no_schema` | Word, **prose only, no schema** | shipment -> delivery notices | 11 | the one-line "identifier: identifier of the order derived from the shipment's list of orders" kind of rule, functional labels instead of field names, a global rule in a far section, a contradiction between two sections. The schemas the author had in mind are in `_hidden/` and **must not be given to the reader**: they evaluate the inferred schema and the guessed rules |
| `wb7_quote_order_docx` | Word, English, formal numbered requirements, schemas in an appendix | quote -> supplier order | 16 | conventions in section 2 (1-based, UTC, rounding), cross-references between requirements, yellow = changed, strike-through = removed, validation that rejects the message, **file name says rev2.2, header says 2.3** |
| `wb8_meter_report_pdf` | PDF (text), pseudo-code close to our own language, schemas supplied as files | meter readings -> report | 11 | running header/footer noise, page break inside the rules, footnotes on a later page, two assignment spellings, two filter syntaxes, 0-based declared in the intro |
| `wb9_multi_mapping` | Excel, **two mappings in one workbook**, global rules in a separate sheet, lookups present | customer -> contact; return -> credit note | 7 + 7 | the reader must ask which mapping; conventions in `ReadMe` and `General rules` (not in the mapping sheets), orange = to confirm, case-insensitive lookups, a row's own default beating a global rule |
| `wb10_scanned_pdf` | PDF **image only** (no text layer), no schema | parcel -> label | 6 | the expected result is a refusal to invent: report "unreadable", ask for OCR or a text version; no tests |

Test files: `tests/caseN.in.json` / `caseN.out.json` generated by a reference implementation of the truth file and validated against the
schemas. WB7 `case3.out.json` is `{"__rejected__": "REQ-16"}` (the fixture's convention for "no order produced"). WB6 tests are in
`_hidden/tests/`. WB9 has one folder per mapping (`customer_to_contact/`, `return_to_credit_note/`) with its own schemas and tests.

All texts in the fixtures and in the code are in English (decided: the reader is exercised on other media and styles, not on other languages; a document in another language is handled as input, not as a fixture).
